char_arithmetic.quote: It does not compile; c is a letter, not a number; so you cannot add 1 to it; Java will give an error that a char and an int cannot be added
char_arithmetic.rule: wrong rule: char is not a numeric type. Right rule: A char is encoded as a 16-bit integer, so arithmetic such as 'b' + 'c' or 'a' + 4 works on the character codes.

paths.label: held
paths.quote: It does not compile; c is a letter, not a number; so you cannot add 1 to it; Java will give an error that a char and an int cannot be added
paths.logic: A char is only a letter, so c + k is an error.
paths.twin_logic: A char is encoded as a 16-bit integer, so arithmetic such as 'b' + 'c' or 'a' + 4 works on the character codes.

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: c is a letter, not a number; so you cannot add 1 to it; Java will give an error that a char and an int cannot be added
paths.logic: In everyday life '7' and 7 are the same thing, and a character is a letter, not a number. A Java char is a 16-bit numeric code: '7' has code 55, and 'a' + 1 is the int 98.

paths.logic: Char arithmetic uses the numeric code stored for each char.
